proposal.title: Guard feed fetches so one bad source cannot interrupt the site
proposal.rootCause: Feed refresh work can be degraded by slow or failing external RSS sources. The root cause is unisolated source failure risk: each source needs its own timeout, catch path, and diagnostic record so one bad feed cannot interrupt the overall news payload.
proposal.proposedFix: Wrap every feed fetch in a bounded timeout and try/catch, return an empty story list for the failed source, record source-level telemetry, and keep the rest of the feeds/cache path running.
proposal.laymanDescription: The Framework believes this change will fix: Feed refresh work can be degraded by slow or failing external RSS sources. The root cause is unisolated source failure risk: each source needs its own timeout, catch path, and diagnostic record so one bad feed cannot interrupt the overall news payload.. It is waiting for owner approval before code is changed.
patchPlan: Add a configurable feed fetch timeout.
Add source-level error tracking in runtime state.
Create a fetchWithTimeout helper.
Update loadFeed so errors return [] and record telemetry instead of throwing.
Expose source failures through feed-status and health diagnostics.
Verify under forced low timeout that feed-status still returns JSON.
proposal.proposedPatch: Owner approval required. After approval, the Brain/AI Framework should apply the structured feed-guard patch directly, then verify /api/feed-status and /api/health?refresh=1. Codex/GitHub should be used only if the Brain needs teaching to create structured patch operations.

Confirm framework proof log records proposal and verification.
proposal.rollbackPlan: Revert only the feed fetch guard changes in server.js if feed loading or diagnostics regress.
proposal.expectedOutcome: Bad or slow external feeds degrade gracefully, are visible in diagnostics, and cannot crash the whole public news path.

proposal.title: Guard feed fetches so one bad source cannot interrupt the site
proposal.rootCause: Feed refresh work can be degraded by slow or failing external RSS sources. The root cause is unisolated source failure risk: each source needs its own timeout, catch path, and diagnostic record so one bad feed cannot interrupt the overall news payload.
proposal.proposedFix: Wrap every feed fetch in a bounded timeout and try/catch, return an empty story list for the failed source, record source-level telemetry, and keep the rest of the feeds/cache path running.
proposal.laymanDescription: The Framework believes this change will fix: Feed refresh work can be degraded by slow or failing external RSS sources. The root cause is unisolated source failure risk: each source needs its own timeout, catch path, and diagnostic record so one bad feed cannot interrupt the overall news payload.. It is waiting for owner approval before code is changed.
patchPlan: Add a configurable feed fetch timeout.
Add source-level error tracking in runtime state.
Create a fetchWithTimeout helper.
Update loadFeed so errors return [] and record telemetry instead of throwing.
Expose source failures through feed-status and health diagnostics.
Verify under forced low timeout that feed-status still returns JSON.
proposal.proposedPatch: Owner approval required. After approval, the Brain/AI Framework should apply the structured feed-guard patch directly, then verify /api/feed-status and /api/health?refresh=1. Codex/GitHub should be used only if the Brain needs teaching to create structured patch operations.

notes: No safe exact structured patch could be generated from this diagnosis.
The Brain should request teaching with target file, exact find text, replacement text, or create/write file content.

verificationPlan: Run node --check server.js.
Start local server with CE_FEED_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS=25.
Call /api/feed-status and confirm JSON response includes source errors instead of endpoint failure.
Run /api/health?refresh=1 and confirm public health responds.
Confirm framework proof log records proposal and verification.
proposal.rollbackPlan: Revert only the feed fetch guard changes in server.js if feed loading or diagnostics regress.
proposal.expectedOutcome: Bad or slow external feeds degrade gracefully, are visible in diagnostics, and cannot crash the whole public news path.

proposal.title: Guard feed fetches so one bad source cannot interrupt the site
proposal.rootCause: Feed refresh work can be degraded by slow or failing external RSS sources. The root cause is unisolated source failure risk: each source needs its own timeout, catch path, and diagnostic record so one bad feed cannot interrupt the overall news payload.
proposal.proposedFix: Wrap every feed fetch in a bounded timeout and try/catch, return an empty story list for the failed source, record source-level telemetry, and keep the rest of the feeds/cache path running.
proposal.laymanDescription: The Framework believes this change will fix: Feed refresh work can be degraded by slow or failing external RSS sources. The root cause is unisolated source failure risk: each source needs its own timeout, catch path, and diagnostic record so one bad feed cannot interrupt the overall news payload.. It is waiting for owner approval before code is changed.
patchPlan: Add a configurable feed fetch timeout.
Add source-level error tracking in runtime state.
Create a fetchWithTimeout helper.
Update loadFeed so errors return [] and record telemetry instead of throwing.
Expose source failures through feed-status and health diagnostics.
Verify under forced low timeout that feed-status still returns JSON.
proposal.proposedPatch: Owner approval required. After approval, the Brain/AI Framework should apply the structured feed-guard patch directly, then verify /api/feed-status and /api/health?refresh=1. Codex/GitHub should be used only if the Brain needs teaching to create structured patch operations.

notes: No safe exact structured patch could be generated from this diagnosis.
The Brain should request teaching with target file, exact find text, replacement text, or create/write file content.

verificationPlan: Run node --check server.js.
Start local server with CE_FEED_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS=25.
Call /api/feed-status and confirm JSON response includes source errors instead of endpoint failure.
Run /api/health?refresh=1 and confirm public health responds.
Confirm framework proof log records proposal and verification.
proposal.rollbackPlan: Revert only the feed fetch guard changes in server.js if feed loading or diagnostics regress.
proposal.expectedOutcome: Bad or slow external feeds degrade gracefully, are visible in diagnostics, and cannot crash the whole public news path.

patchPlan: Add a configurable feed fetch timeout.
Add source-level error tracking in runtime state.
Create a fetchWithTimeout helper.

proposal.laymanDescription: The Framework believes this change will fix: Feed refresh work can be degraded by slow or failing external RSS sources. The root cause is unisolated source failure risk: each source needs its own timeout, catch path, and diagnostic record so one bad feed cannot interrupt the overall news payload.. It is waiting for owner approval before code is changed.
patchPlan: Add a configurable feed fetch timeout.
Add source-level error tracking in runtime state.
Create a fetchWithTimeout helper.
Update loadFeed so errors return [] and record telemetry instead of throwing.
Expose source failures through feed-status and health diagnostics.
Verify under forced low timeout that feed-status still returns JSON.
proposal.proposedPatch: Owner approval required. After approval, the Brain/AI Framework should apply the structured feed-guard patch directly, then verify /api/feed-status and /api/health?refresh=1. Codex/GitHub should be used only if the Brain needs teaching to create structured patch operations.

notes: No safe exact structured patch could be generated from this diagnosis.
The Brain should request teaching with target file, exact find text, replacement text, or create/write file content.

verificationPlan: Run node --check server.js.
Start local server with CE_FEED_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS=25.
Call /api/feed-status and confirm JSON response includes source errors instead of endpoint failure.
Run /api/health?refresh=1 and confirm public health responds.
Confirm framework proof log records proposal and verification.
proposal.rollbackPlan: Revert only the feed fetch guard changes in server.js if feed loading or diagnostics regress.
proposal.expectedOutcome: Bad or slow external feeds degrade gracefully, are visible in diagnostics, and cannot crash the whole public news path.

proposal.title: Guard feed fetches so one bad source cannot interrupt the site
proposal.rootCause: Feed refresh work can be degraded by slow or failing external RSS sources. The root cause is unisolated source failure risk: each source needs its own timeout, catch path, and diagnostic record so one bad feed cannot interrupt the overall news payload.
proposal.proposedFix: Wrap every feed fetch in a bounded timeout and try/catch, return an empty story list for the failed source, record source-level telemetry, and keep the rest of the feeds/cache path running.
proposal.laymanDescription: The Framework believes this change will fix: Feed refresh work can be degraded by slow or failing external RSS sources. The root cause is unisolated source failure risk: each source needs its own timeout, catch path, and diagnostic record so one bad feed cannot interrupt the overall news payload.. It is waiting for owner approval before code is changed.
patchPlan: Add a configurable feed fetch timeout.
Add source-level error tracking in runtime state.
Create a fetchWithTimeout helper.
Update loadFeed so errors return [] and record telemetry instead of throwing.
Expose source failures through feed-status and health diagnostics.
Verify under forced low timeout that feed-status still returns JSON.
proposal.proposedPatch: Owner approval required. After approval, the Brain/AI Framework should apply the structured feed-guard patch directly, then verify /api/feed-status and /api/health?refresh=1. Codex/GitHub should be used only if the Brain needs teaching to create structured patch operations.

notes: No safe exact structured patch could be generated from this diagnosis.
The Brain should request teaching with target file, exact find text, replacement text, or create/write file content.

verificationPlan: Run node --check server.js.
Start local server with CE_FEED_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS=25.
Call /api/feed-status and confirm JSON response includes source errors instead of endpoint failure.
Run /api/health?refresh=1 and confirm public health responds.
Confirm framework proof log records proposal and verification.
proposal.rollbackPlan: Revert only the feed fetch guard changes in server.js if feed loading or diagnostics regress.
proposal.expectedOutcome: Bad or slow external feeds degrade gracefully, are visible in diagnostics, and cannot crash the whole public news path.

proposal.title: Guard feed fetches so one bad source cannot interrupt the site
proposal.rootCause: Feed refresh work can be degraded by slow or failing external RSS sources. The root cause is unisolated source failure risk: each source needs its own timeout, catch path, and diagnostic record so one bad feed cannot interrupt the overall news payload.
proposal.proposedFix: Wrap every feed fetch in a bounded timeout and try/catch, return an empty story list for the failed source, record source-level telemetry, and keep the rest of the feeds/cache path running.
proposal.laymanDescription: The Framework believes this change will fix: Feed refresh work can be degraded by slow or failing external RSS sources. The root cause is unisolated source failure risk: each source needs its own timeout, catch path, and diagnostic record so one bad feed cannot interrupt the overall news payload.. It is waiting for owner approval before code is changed.
patchPlan: Add a configurable feed fetch timeout.
Add source-level error tracking in runtime state.
Create a fetchWithTimeout helper.
Update loadFeed so errors return [] and record telemetry instead of throwing.
Expose source failures through feed-status and health diagnostics.
Verify under forced low timeout that feed-status still returns JSON.
proposal.proposedPatch: Owner approval required. After approval, the Brain/AI Framework should apply the structured feed-guard patch directly, then verify /api/feed-status and /api/health?refresh=1. Codex/GitHub should be used only if the Brain needs teaching to create structured patch operations.

notes: No safe exact structured patch could be generated from this diagnosis.
The Brain should request teaching with target file, exact find text, replacement text, or create/write file content.

verificationPlan: Run node --check server.js.
Start local server with CE_FEED_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS=25.
Call /api/feed-status and confirm JSON response includes source errors instead of endpoint failure.
Run /api/health?refresh=1 and confirm public health responds.
Confirm framework proof log records proposal and verification.
proposal.rollbackPlan: Revert only the feed fetch guard changes in server.js if feed loading or diagnostics regress.
proposal.expectedOutcome: Bad or slow external feeds degrade gracefully, are visible in diagnostics, and cannot crash the whole public news path.

proposal.title: Guard feed fetches so one bad source cannot interrupt the site
proposal.rootCause: Feed refresh work can be degraded by slow or failing external RSS sources. The root cause is unisolated source failure risk: each source needs its own timeout, catch path, and diagnostic record so one bad feed cannot interrupt the overall news payload.
proposal.proposedFix: Wrap every feed fetch in a bounded timeout and try/catch, return an empty story list for the failed source, record source-level telemetry, and keep the rest of the feeds/cache path running.
proposal.laymanDescription: The Framework believes this change will fix: Feed refresh work can be degraded by slow or failing external RSS sources. The root cause is unisolated source failure risk: each source needs its own timeout, catch path, and diagnostic record so one bad feed cannot interrupt the overall news payload.. It is waiting for owner approval before code is changed.
patchPlan: Add a configurable feed fetch timeout.
Add source-level error tracking in runtime state.
Create a fetchWithTimeout helper.
Update loadFeed so errors return [] and record telemetry instead of throwing.
Expose source failures through feed-status and health diagnostics.
Verify under forced low timeout that feed-status still returns JSON.
proposal.proposedPatch: Owner approval required. After approval, the Brain/AI Framework should apply the structured feed-guard patch directly, then verify /api/feed-status and /api/health?refresh=1. Codex/GitHub should be used only if the Brain needs teaching to create structured patch operations.

notes: No safe exact structured patch could be generated from this diagnosis.
The Brain should request teaching with target file, exact find text, replacement text, or create/write file content.

verificationPlan: Run node --check server.js.
Start local server with CE_FEED_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS=25.
Call /api/feed-status and confirm JSON response includes source errors instead of endpoint failure.
Run /api/health?refresh=1 and confirm public health responds.
Confirm framework proof log records proposal and verification.
proposal.rollbackPlan: Revert only the feed fetch guard changes in server.js if feed loading or diagnostics regress.
proposal.expectedOutcome: Bad or slow external feeds degrade gracefully, are visible in diagnostics, and cannot crash the whole public news path.

proposal.title: Guard feed fetches so one bad source cannot interrupt the site
proposal.rootCause: Feed refresh work can be degraded by slow or failing external RSS sources. The root cause is unisolated source failure risk: each source needs its own timeout, catch path, and diagnostic record so one bad feed cannot interrupt the overall news payload.
proposal.proposedFix: Wrap every feed fetch in a bounded timeout and try/catch, return an empty story list for the failed source, record source-level telemetry, and keep the rest of the feeds/cache path running.
proposal.laymanDescription: The Framework believes this change will fix: Feed refresh work can be degraded by slow or failing external RSS sources. The root cause is unisolated source failure risk: each source needs its own timeout, catch path, and diagnostic record so one bad feed cannot interrupt the overall news payload.. It is waiting for owner approval before code is changed.
patchPlan: Add a configurable feed fetch timeout.
Add source-level error tracking in runtime state.
Create a fetchWithTimeout helper.
Update loadFeed so errors return [] and record telemetry instead of throwing.
Expose source failures through feed-status and health diagnostics.
Verify under forced low timeout that feed-status still returns JSON.
proposal.proposedPatch: Owner approval required. After approval, the Brain/AI Framework should apply the structured feed-guard patch directly, then verify /api/feed-status and /api/health?refresh=1. Codex/GitHub should be used only if the Brain needs teaching to create structured patch operations.

notes: No safe exact structured patch could be generated from this diagnosis.
The Brain should request teaching with target file, exact find text, replacement text, or create/write file content.

verificationPlan: Run node --check server.js.
Start local server with CE_FEED_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS=25.
Call /api/feed-status and confirm JSON response includes source errors instead of endpoint failure.
Run /api/health?refresh=1 and confirm public health responds.
Confirm framework proof log records proposal and verification.
proposal.rollbackPlan: Revert only the feed fetch guard changes in server.js if feed loading or diagnostics regress.
proposal.expectedOutcome: Bad or slow external feeds degrade gracefully, are visible in diagnostics, and cannot crash the whole public news path.

proposal.title: Guard feed fetches so one bad source cannot interrupt the site
proposal.rootCause: Feed refresh work can be degraded by slow or failing external RSS sources. The root cause is unisolated source failure risk: each source needs its own timeout, catch path, and diagnostic record so one bad feed cannot interrupt the overall news payload.
proposal.proposedFix: Wrap every feed fetch in a bounded timeout and try/catch, return an empty story list for the failed source, record source-level telemetry, and keep the rest of the feeds/cache path running.
proposal.laymanDescription: The Framework believes this change will fix: Feed refresh work can be degraded by slow or failing external RSS sources. The root cause is unisolated source failure risk: each source needs its own timeout, catch path, and diagnostic record so one bad feed cannot interrupt the overall news payload.. It is waiting for owner approval before code is changed.
patchPlan: Add a configurable feed fetch timeout.
Add source-level error tracking in runtime state.
Create a fetchWithTimeout helper.
Update loadFeed so errors return [] and record telemetry instead of throwing.
Expose source failures through feed-status and health diagnostics.
Verify under forced low timeout that feed-status still returns JSON.
proposal.proposedPatch: Owner approval required. After approval, the Brain/AI Framework should apply the structured feed-guard patch directly, then verify /api/feed-status and /api/health?refresh=1. Codex/GitHub should be used only if the Brain needs teaching to create structured patch operations.

notes: No safe exact structured patch could be generated from this diagnosis.
The Brain should request teaching with target file, exact find text, replacement text, or create/write file content.

verificationPlan: Run node --check server.js.
Start local server with CE_FEED_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS=25.
Call /api/feed-status and confirm JSON response includes source errors instead of endpoint failure.
Run /api/health?refresh=1 and confirm public health responds.
Confirm framework proof log records proposal and verification.
proposal.rollbackPlan: Revert only the feed fetch guard changes in server.js if feed loading or diagnostics regress.
proposal.expectedOutcome: Bad or slow external feeds degrade gracefully, are visible in diagnostics, and cannot crash the whole public news path.

proposal.title: Guard feed fetches so one bad source cannot interrupt the site
proposal.rootCause: Feed refresh work can be degraded by slow or failing external RSS sources. The root cause is unisolated source failure risk: each source needs its own timeout, catch path, and diagnostic record so one bad feed cannot interrupt the overall news payload.
proposal.proposedFix: Wrap every feed fetch in a bounded timeout and try/catch, return an empty story list for the failed source, record source-level telemetry, and keep the rest of the feeds/cache path running.
proposal.laymanDescription: The Framework believes this change will fix: Feed refresh work can be degraded by slow or failing external RSS sources. The root cause is unisolated source failure risk: each source needs its own timeout, catch path, and diagnostic record so one bad feed cannot interrupt the overall news payload.. It is waiting for owner approval before code is changed.
patchPlan: Add a configurable feed fetch timeout.
Add source-level error tracking in runtime state.
Create a fetchWithTimeout helper.
Update loadFeed so errors return [] and record telemetry instead of throwing.
Expose source failures through feed-status and health diagnostics.
Verify under forced low timeout that feed-status still returns JSON.
proposal.proposedPatch: Owner approval required. After approval, the Brain/AI Framework should apply the structured feed-guard patch directly, then verify /api/feed-status and /api/health?refresh=1. Codex/GitHub should be used only if the Brain needs teaching to create structured patch operations.

notes: No safe exact structured patch could be generated from this diagnosis.
The Brain should request teaching with target file, exact find text, replacement text, or create/write file content.

verificationPlan: Run node --check server.js.
Start local server with CE_FEED_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS=25.
Call /api/feed-status and confirm JSON response includes source errors instead of endpoint failure.
Run /api/health?refresh=1 and confirm public health responds.
Confirm framework proof log records proposal and verification.
proposal.rollbackPlan: Revert only the feed fetch guard changes in server.js if feed loading or diagnostics regress.
proposal.expectedOutcome: Bad or slow external feeds degrade gracefully, are visible in diagnostics, and cannot crash the whole public news path.

# Codex Teaching Direction

Patch ID: patch_proposal_1782782939279_urhsml

## Owner Intent
The AI Framework/Brain could not complete this safely on its own, or needs Codex teaching before it can execute this pattern independently in the future. Teach the Framework the missing method, then make the smallest safe code change needed.

## Title
Guard feed fetches so one bad source cannot interrupt the site

## Plain-English Summary
The Framework believes this change will fix: Feed refresh work can be degraded by slow or failing external RSS sources. The root cause is unisolated source failure risk: each source needs its own timeout, catch path, and diagnostic record so one bad feed cannot interrupt the overall news payload.. It is waiting for owner approval before code is changed.

## Root Cause
Feed refresh work can be degraded by slow or failing external RSS sources. The root cause is unisolated source failure risk: each source needs its own timeout, catch path, and diagnostic record so one bad feed cannot interrupt the overall news payload.

## Requested Fix
Wrap every feed fetch in a bounded timeout and try/catch, return an empty story list for the failed source, record source-level telemetry, and keep the rest of the feeds/cache path running.

## Affected Files
- server.js

## Verification Required
- Run node --check server.js.
- Start local server with CE_FEED_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS=25.
- Call /api/feed-status and confirm JSON response includes source errors instead of endpoint failure.
- Run /api/health?refresh=1 and confirm public health responds.
- Confirm framework proof log records proposal and verification.

## Rollback
Revert only the feed fetch guard changes in server.js if feed loading or diagnostics regress.

## Title
Guard feed fetches so one bad source cannot interrupt the site

## Plain-English Summary
The Framework believes this change will fix: Feed refresh work can be degraded by slow or failing external RSS sources. The root cause is unisolated source failure risk: each source needs its own timeout, catch path, and diagnostic record so one bad feed cannot interrupt the overall news payload.. ## Root Cause
Feed refresh work can be degraded by slow or failing external RSS sources. The root cause is unisolated source failure risk: each source needs its own timeout, catch path, and diagnostic record so one bad feed cannot interrupt the overall news payload.

## Requested Fix
Wrap every feed fetch in a bounded timeout and try/catch, return an empty story list for the failed source, record source-level telemetry, and keep the rest of the feeds/cache path running.

- server.js

- Call /api/feed-status and confirm JSON response includes source errors instead of endpoint failure.
- Run /api/health?refresh=1 and confirm public health responds.
- Confirm framework proof log records proposal and verification.

## Rollback
Revert only the feed fetch guard changes in server.js if feed loading or diagnostics regress.

The AI Framework/Brain could not complete this safely on its own, or needs Codex teaching before it can execute this pattern independently in the future. Teach the Framework the missing method, then make the smallest safe code change needed.

## Title
Guard feed fetches so one bad source cannot interrupt the site

## Plain-English Summary
The Framework believes this change will fix: Feed refresh work can be degraded by slow or failing external RSS sources. The root cause is unisolated source failure risk: each source needs its own timeout, catch path, and diagnostic record so one bad feed cannot interrupt the overall news payload.. It is waiting for owner approval before code is changed.

## Root Cause
Feed refresh work can be degraded by slow or failing external RSS sources. The root cause is unisolated source failure risk: each source needs its own timeout, catch path, and diagnostic record so one bad feed cannot interrupt the overall news payload.

## Requested Fix
Wrap every feed fetch in a bounded timeout and try/catch, return an empty story list for the failed source, record source-level telemetry, and keep the rest of the feeds/cache path running.

## Affected Files
- server.js

## Verification Required
- Run node --check server.js.
- Start local server with CE_FEED_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS=25.
- Call /api/feed-status and confirm JSON response includes source errors instead of endpoint failure.
- Run /api/health?refresh=1 and confirm public health responds.
- Confirm framework proof log records proposal and verification.

## Rollback
Revert only the feed fetch guard changes in server.js if feed loading or diagnostics regress.

## Framework Learning Requirement
The Brain could not safely generate structured filePatches from this diagnosis yet. Codex/GitHub should teach the missing exact file path, find text, replacement text, or create/write operation.

# Codex Teaching Direction

Patch ID: patch_proposal_1782782939279_urhsml
Status: pending-owner-approval
Risk: medium

## Owner Intent
The AI Framework/Brain could not complete this safely on its own, or needs Codex teaching before it can execute this pattern independently in the future. Teach the Framework the missing method, then make the smallest safe code change needed.

## Title
Guard feed fetches so one bad source cannot interrupt the site

## Plain-English Summary
The Framework believes this change will fix: Feed refresh work can be degraded by slow or failing external RSS sources. The root cause is unisolated source failure risk: each source needs its own timeout, catch path, and diagnostic record so one bad feed cannot interrupt the overall news payload.. It is waiting for owner approval before code is changed.

## Root Cause
Feed refresh work can be degraded by slow or failing external RSS sources. The root cause is unisolated source failure risk: each source needs its own timeout, catch path, and diagnostic record so one bad feed cannot interrupt the overall news payload.

## Requested Fix
Wrap every feed fetch in a bounded timeout and try/catch, return an empty story list for the failed source, record source-level telemetry, and keep the rest of the feeds/cache path running.

## Affected Files
- server.js

## Verification Required
- Run node --check server.js.
- Start local server with CE_FEED_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS=25.
- Call /api/feed-status and confirm JSON response includes source errors instead of endpoint failure.
- Run /api/health?refresh=1 and confirm public health responds.
- Confirm framework proof log records proposal and verification.

## Rollback
Revert only the feed fetch guard changes in server.js if feed loading or diagnostics regress.

## Framework Learning Requirement

1. Explain why the Brain could not complete the patch, if applicable.

# Codex Teaching Direction

Patch ID: patch_proposal_1782782939279_urhsml
Status: pending-owner-approval
Risk: medium

## Owner Intent
The AI Framework/Brain could not complete this safely on its own, or needs Codex teaching before it can execute this pattern independently in the future. Teach the Framework the missing method, then make the smallest safe code change needed.

## Title
Guard feed fetches so one bad source cannot interrupt the site

## Plain-English Summary
The Framework believes this change will fix: Feed refresh work can be degraded by slow or failing external RSS sources. The root cause is unisolated source failure risk: each source needs its own timeout, catch path, and diagnostic record so one bad feed cannot interrupt the overall news payload.. It is waiting for owner approval before code is changed.

## Root Cause
Feed refresh work can be degraded by slow or failing external RSS sources. The root cause is unisolated source failure risk: each source needs its own timeout, catch path, and diagnostic record so one bad feed cannot interrupt the overall news payload.

## Requested Fix
Wrap every feed fetch in a bounded timeout and try/catch, return an empty story list for the failed source, record source-level telemetry, and keep the rest of the feeds/cache path running.

## Affected Files
- server.js

## Verification Required
- Run node --check server.js.
- Start local server with CE_FEED_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS=25.
- Call /api/feed-status and confirm JSON response includes source errors instead of endpoint failure.
- Run /api/health?refresh=1 and confirm public health responds.
- Confirm framework proof log records proposal and verification.

## Rollback
Revert only the feed fetch guard changes in server.js if feed loading or diagnostics regress.

## Framework Learning Requirement
The Brain could not safely generate structured filePatches from this diagnosis yet. Codex/GitHub should teach the missing exact file path, find text, replacement text, or create/write operation.


## Expected Codex Response
1. Explain why the Brain could not complete the patch, if applicable.
2. Apply or teach the exact structured patch operation.
3. Run the listed verification checks.
4. Record what the Framework should learn so future similar patches can be applied by the Brain after owner approval.

# Codex Teaching Direction

Patch ID: patch_proposal_1782782939279_urhsml
Status: pending-owner-approval
Risk: medium

## Owner Intent
The AI Framework/Brain could not complete this safely on its own, or needs Codex teaching before it can execute this pattern independently in the future. Teach the Framework the missing method, then make the smallest safe code change needed.

## Title
Guard feed fetches so one bad source cannot interrupt the site

## Plain-English Summary
The Framework believes this change will fix: Feed refresh work can be degraded by slow or failing external RSS sources. The root cause is unisolated source failure risk: each source needs its own timeout, catch path, and diagnostic record so one bad feed cannot interrupt the overall news payload.. It is waiting for owner approval before code is changed.

## Root Cause
Feed refresh work can be degraded by slow or failing external RSS sources. The root cause is unisolated source failure risk: each source needs its own timeout, catch path, and diagnostic record so one bad feed cannot interrupt the overall news payload.

## Requested Fix
Wrap every feed fetch in a bounded timeout and try/catch, return an empty story list for the failed source, record source-level telemetry, and keep the rest of the feeds/cache path running.

## Affected Files
- server.js

## Verification Required
- Run node --check server.js.
- Start local server with CE_FEED_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS=25.
- Call /api/feed-status and confirm JSON response includes source errors instead of endpoint failure.
- Run /api/health?refresh=1 and confirm public health responds.
- Confirm framework proof log records proposal and verification.

## Rollback
Revert only the feed fetch guard changes in server.js if feed loading or diagnostics regress.

# Codex Teaching Direction

Patch ID: patch_proposal_1782782939279_urhsml
Status: pending-owner-approval
Risk: medium

## Owner Intent
The AI Framework/Brain could not complete this safely on its own, or needs Codex teaching before it can execute this pattern independently in the future. Teach the Framework the missing method, then make the smallest safe code change needed.

## Title
Guard feed fetches so one bad source cannot interrupt the site

## Plain-English Summary
The Framework believes this change will fix: Feed refresh work can be degraded by slow or failing external RSS sources. The root cause is unisolated source failure risk: each source needs its own timeout, catch path, and diagnostic record so one bad feed cannot interrupt the overall news payload.. It is waiting for owner approval before code is changed.

## Root Cause
Feed refresh work can be degraded by slow or failing external RSS sources. The root cause is unisolated source failure risk: each source needs its own timeout, catch path, and diagnostic record so one bad feed cannot interrupt the overall news payload.

## Requested Fix
Wrap every feed fetch in a bounded timeout and try/catch, return an empty story list for the failed source, record source-level telemetry, and keep the rest of the feeds/cache path running.

## Affected Files
- server.js

## Verification Required
- Run node --check server.js.
- Start local server with CE_FEED_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS=25.
- Call /api/feed-status and confirm JSON response includes source errors instead of endpoint failure.
- Run /api/health?refresh=1 and confirm public health responds.
- Confirm framework proof log records proposal and verification.

## Rollback
Revert only the feed fetch guard changes in server.js if feed loading or diagnostics regress.

## Framework Learning Requirement
The Brain could not safely generate structured filePatches from this diagnosis yet. Codex/GitHub should teach the missing exact file path, find text, replacement text, or create/write operation.


## Expected Codex Response
1. Explain why the Brain could not complete the patch, if applicable.
2. Apply or teach the exact structured patch operation.
3. Run the listed verification checks.
4. Record what the Framework should learn so future similar patches can be applied by the Brain after owner approval.

# Codex Teaching Direction

Patch ID: patch_proposal_1782782939279_urhsml
Status: pending-owner-approval
Risk: medium

## Owner Intent
The AI Framework/Brain could not complete this safely on its own, or needs Codex teaching before it can execute this pattern independently in the future. Teach the Framework the missing method, then make the smallest safe code change needed.

## Title
Guard feed fetches so one bad source cannot interrupt the site

## Plain-English Summary
The Framework believes this change will fix: Feed refresh work can be degraded by slow or failing external RSS sources. The root cause is unisolated source failure risk: each source needs its own timeout, catch path, and diagnostic record so one bad feed cannot interrupt the overall news payload.. It is waiting for owner approval before code is changed.

## Root Cause
Feed refresh work can be degraded by slow or failing external RSS sources. The root cause is unisolated source failure risk: each source needs its own timeout, catch path, and diagnostic record so one bad feed cannot interrupt the overall news payload.

## Requested Fix
Wrap every feed fetch in a bounded timeout and try/catch, return an empty story list for the failed source, record source-level telemetry, and keep the rest of the feeds/cache path running.

## Affected Files
- server.js

## Verification Required
- Run node --check server.js.
- Start local server with CE_FEED_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS=25.
- Call /api/feed-status and confirm JSON response includes source errors instead of endpoint failure.
- Run /api/health?refresh=1 and confirm public health responds.
- Confirm framework proof log records proposal and verification.

## Rollback
Revert only the feed fetch guard changes in server.js if feed loading or diagnostics regress.

## Framework Learning Requirement
The Brain could not safely generate structured filePatches from this diagnosis yet. Codex/GitHub should teach the missing exact file path, find text, replacement text, or create/write operation.


## Expected Codex Response
1. Explain why the Brain could not complete the patch, if applicable.
2. Apply or teach the exact structured patch operation.
3. Run the listed verification checks.
4. Record what the Framework should learn so future similar patches can be applied by the Brain after owner approval.

# Codex Teaching Direction

Patch ID: patch_proposal_1782782939279_urhsml
Status: pending-owner-approval
Risk: medium

## Owner Intent
The AI Framework/Brain could not complete this safely on its own, or needs Codex teaching before it can execute this pattern independently in the future. Teach the Framework the missing method, then make the smallest safe code change needed.

## Title
Guard feed fetches so one bad source cannot interrupt the site

## Plain-English Summary
The Framework believes this change will fix: Feed refresh work can be degraded by slow or failing external RSS sources. The root cause is unisolated source failure risk: each source needs its own timeout, catch path, and diagnostic record so one bad feed cannot interrupt the overall news payload.. It is waiting for owner approval before code is changed.

## Root Cause
Feed refresh work can be degraded by slow or failing external RSS sources. The root cause is unisolated source failure risk: each source needs its own timeout, catch path, and diagnostic record so one bad feed cannot interrupt the overall news payload.

## Requested Fix
Wrap every feed fetch in a bounded timeout and try/catch, return an empty story list for the failed source, record source-level telemetry, and keep the rest of the feeds/cache path running.

## Affected Files
- server.js

## Verification Required
- Run node --check server.js.
- Start local server with CE_FEED_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS=25.
- Call /api/feed-status and confirm JSON response includes source errors instead of endpoint failure.
- Run /api/health?refresh=1 and confirm public health responds.
- Confirm framework proof log records proposal and verification.

## Rollback
Revert only the feed fetch guard changes in server.js if feed loading or diagnostics regress.

## Framework Learning Requirement
The Brain could not safely generate structured filePatches from this diagnosis yet. Codex/GitHub should teach the missing exact file path, find text, replacement text, or create/write operation.


## Expected Codex Response
1. Explain why the Brain could not complete the patch, if applicable.
2. Apply or teach the exact structured patch operation.
3. Run the listed verification checks.
4. Record what the Framework should learn so future similar patches can be applied by the Brain after owner approval.

proposal.rootCause: Feed refresh work can be degraded by slow or failing external RSS sources. The root cause is unisolated source failure risk: each source needs its own timeout, catch path, and diagnostic record so one bad feed cannot interrupt the overall news payload.
proposal.proposedFix: Wrap every feed fetch in a bounded timeout and try/catch, return an empty story list for the failed source, record source-level telemetry, and keep the rest of the feeds/cache path running.

proposal.codexDirection:
# Codex Teaching Direction

Patch ID: patch_proposal_1782782939279_urhsml
Status: pending-owner-approval
Risk: medium

## Owner Intent
The AI Framework/Brain could not complete this safely on its own, or needs Codex teaching before it can execute this pattern independently in the future. Teach the Framework the missing method, then make the smallest safe code change needed.

## Title
Guard feed fetches so one bad source cannot interrupt the site

## Plain-English Summary
The Framework believes this change will fix: Feed refresh work can be degraded by slow or failing external RSS sources. The root cause is unisolated source failure risk: each source needs its own timeout, catch path, and diagnostic record so one bad feed cannot interrupt the overall news payload.. It is waiting for owner approval before code is changed.

## Root Cause
Feed refresh work can be degraded by slow or failing external RSS sources. The root cause is unisolated source failure risk: each source needs its own timeout, catch path, and diagnostic record so one bad feed cannot interrupt the overall news payload.

## Requested Fix
Wrap every feed fetch in a bounded timeout and try/catch, return an empty story list for the failed source, record source-level telemetry, and keep the rest of the feeds/cache path running.

## Affected Files
- server.js

## Verification Required
- Run node --check server.js.
- Start local server with CE_FEED_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS=25.
- Call /api/feed-status and confirm JSON response includes source errors instead of endpoint failure.
- Run /api/health?refresh=1 and confirm public health responds.
- Confirm framework proof log records proposal and verification.

## Rollback
Revert only the feed fetch guard changes in server.js if feed loading or diagnostics regress.

## Framework Learning Requirement
The Brain could not safely generate structured filePatches from this diagnosis yet. Codex/GitHub should teach the missing exact file path, find text, replacement text, or create/write operation.


## Expected Codex Response
1. Explain why the Brain could not complete the patch, if applicable.
2. Apply or teach the exact structured patch operation.
3. Run the listed verification checks.
4. Record what the Framework should learn so future similar patches can be applied by the Brain after owner approval.

proposal.title: Guard feed fetches so one bad source cannot interrupt the site
proposal.rootCause: Feed refresh work can be degraded by slow or failing external RSS sources. The root cause is unisolated source failure risk: each source needs its own timeout, catch path, and diagnostic record so one bad feed cannot interrupt the overall news payload.
proposal.proposedFix: Wrap every feed fetch in a bounded timeout and try/catch, return an empty story list for the failed source, record source-level telemetry, and keep the rest of the feeds/cache path running.

The root cause is unisolated source failure risk: each source needs its own timeout, catch path, and diagnostic record so one bad feed cannot interrupt the overall news payload.. It is waiting for owner approval before code is changed.
patchPlan: Add a configurable feed fetch timeout.
Add source-level error tracking in runtime state.
Create a fetchWithTimeout helper.
Update loadFeed so errors return [] and record telemetry instead of throwing.

Verify under forced low timeout that feed-status still returns JSON.

proposal.codexDirection:
# Codex Teaching Direction

Patch ID: patch_proposal_1782782939279_urhsml
Status: pending-owner-approval
Risk: medium

## Owner Intent
The AI Framework/Brain could not complete this safely on its own, or needs Codex teaching before it can execute this pattern independently in the future. Teach the Framework the missing method, then make the smallest safe code change needed.

## Title
Guard feed fetches so one bad source cannot interrupt the site

## Plain-English Summary
The Framework believes this change will fix: Feed refresh work can be degraded by slow or failing external RSS sources. The root cause is unisolated source failure risk: each source needs its own timeout, catch path, and diagnostic record so one bad feed cannot interrupt the overall news payload.. It is waiting for owner approval before code is changed.

## Root Cause
Feed refresh work can be degraded by slow or failing external RSS sources. The root cause is unisolated source failure risk: each source needs its own timeout, catch path, and diagnostic record so one bad feed cannot interrupt the overall news payload.

## Requested Fix
Wrap every feed fetch in a bounded timeout and try/catch, return an empty story list for the failed source, record source-level telemetry, and keep the rest of the feeds/cache path running.

## Affected Files
- server.js

## Verification Required
- Run node --check server.js.
- Start local server with CE_FEED_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS=25.
- Call /api/feed-status and confirm JSON response includes source errors instead of endpoint failure.
- Run /api/health?refresh=1 and confirm public health responds.
- Confirm framework proof log records proposal and verification.

## Rollback
Revert only the feed fetch guard changes in server.js if feed loading or diagnostics regress.

## Framework Learning Requirement

## Expected Codex Response
1. Explain why the Brain could not complete the patch, if applicable.
2. Apply or teach the exact structured patch operation.
3. Run the listed verification checks.
4. Record what the Framework should learn so future similar patches can be applied by the Brain after owner approval.

## Title
Guard feed fetches so one bad source cannot interrupt the site

## Plain-English Summary
The Framework believes this change will fix: Feed refresh work can be degraded by slow or failing external RSS sources. The root cause is unisolated source failure risk: each source needs its own timeout, catch path, and diagnostic record so one bad feed cannot interrupt the overall news payload.. ## Root Cause
Feed refresh work can be degraded by slow or failing external RSS sources. The root cause is unisolated source failure risk: each source needs its own timeout, catch path, and diagnostic record so one bad feed cannot interrupt the overall news payload.

## Requested Fix
Wrap every feed fetch in a bounded timeout and try/catch, return an empty story list for the failed source, record source-level telemetry, and keep the rest of the feeds/cache path running.

- server.js

- Call /api/feed-status and confirm JSON response includes source errors instead of endpoint failure.
- Run /api/health?refresh=1 and confirm public health responds.
- Confirm framework proof log records proposal and verification.

## Rollback
Revert only the feed fetch guard changes in server.js if feed loading or diagnostics regress.

proposal.rootCause: Feed refresh work can be degraded by slow or failing external RSS sources. The root cause is unisolated source failure risk: each source needs its own timeout, catch path, and diagnostic record so one bad feed cannot interrupt the overall news payload.
proposal.proposedFix: Wrap every feed fetch in a bounded timeout and try/catch, return an empty story list for the failed source, record source-level telemetry, and keep the rest of the feeds/cache path running.

Add source-level error tracking in runtime state.
Create a fetchWithTimeout helper.
Update loadFeed so errors return [] and record telemetry instead of throwing.

Verify under forced low timeout that feed-status still returns JSON.

proposal.codexDirection:
# Codex Teaching Direction

Patch ID: patch_proposal_1782782939279_urhsml
Status: pending-owner-approval
Risk: medium

## Owner Intent
The AI Framework/Brain could not complete this safely on its own, or needs Codex teaching before it can execute this pattern independently in the future. Teach the Framework the missing method, then make the smallest safe code change needed.

## Title
Guard feed fetches so one bad source cannot interrupt the site

## Plain-English Summary
The Framework believes this change will fix: Feed refresh work can be degraded by slow or failing external RSS sources. The root cause is unisolated source failure risk: each source needs its own timeout, catch path, and diagnostic record so one bad feed cannot interrupt the overall news payload.. It is waiting for owner approval before code is changed.

## Root Cause
Feed refresh work can be degraded by slow or failing external RSS sources. The root cause is unisolated source failure risk: each source needs its own timeout, catch path, and diagnostic record so one bad feed cannot interrupt the overall news payload.

## Requested Fix
Wrap every feed fetch in a bounded timeout and try/catch, return an empty story list for the failed source, record source-level telemetry, and keep the rest of the feeds/cache path running.

## Affected Files
- server.js

## Verification Required
- Run node --check server.js.
- Start local server with CE_FEED_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS=25.
- Call /api/feed-status and confirm JSON response includes source errors instead of endpoint failure.
- Run /api/health?refresh=1 and confirm public health responds.
- Confirm framework proof log records proposal and verification.

## Rollback
Revert only the feed fetch guard changes in server.js if feed loading or diagnostics regress.

## Framework Learning Requirement
The Brain could not safely generate structured filePatches from this diagnosis yet. Codex/GitHub should teach the missing exact file path, find text, replacement text, or create/write operation.


## Expected Codex Response
1. Explain why the Brain could not complete the patch, if applicable.
2. Apply or teach the exact structured patch operation.
3. Run the listed verification checks.
4. Record what the Framework should learn so future similar patches can be applied by the Brain after owner approval.

Record Industry Proposes Labels for AI-Generated Music
approvedPatterns.summary: Music-industry groups are proposing voluntary labels for AI-generated and AI-assisted recordings so listeners can better understand how generative tools were used in songs.
approvedPatterns.articleSummary: Music-industry groups are proposing voluntary labels for recordings made with generative AI so listeners can distinguish fully AI-generated tracks from songs where human artists used AI assistance. The proposal comes from organizations including the Recording Industry Association of America, the Recording Academy, SAG-AFTRA, and other music groups that want a unified labeling approach for streaming services and other platforms. Under the proposal, a large AI label would identify fully AI-generated recordings, while a smaller ai marker would flag songs where AI was used as a tool in the creative process. Industry leaders said the goal is transparency as AI-generated uploads increase and artists, labels, platforms, and fans debate how authorship should be identified. The timing and platform adoption remain unresolved. Streaming services would still need to decide whether to use the labels and how the markers would appear to listeners.
body: Music-industry groups are proposing voluntary labels for recordings made with generative AI so listeners can distinguish fully AI-generated tracks from songs where human artists used AI assistance.

The proposal comes from organizations including the Recording Industry Association of America, the Recording Academy, SAG-AFTRA, and other music groups that want a unified labeling approach for streaming services and other platforms.
Under the proposal, a large AI label would identify fully AI-generated recordings, while a smaller ai marker would flag songs where AI was used as a tool in the creative process.
Industry leaders said the goal is transparency as AI-generated uploads increase and artists, labels, platforms, and fans debate how authorship should be identified.
The timing and platform adoption remain unresolved. Streaming services would still need to decide whether to use the labels and how the markers would appear to listeners.

writingPatternLibrary.philosophy: Learn reusable writing techniques, not article content or publisher expression.
boundaries: Do not memorize article bodies, publisher phrasing, or publisher headline structure.
Store craft principles, issue frequencies, success rates, and prevention rules only.

writingPatternLibrary.writerDirective: Before drafting, read the Story Dossier for facts and this pattern library for craft. Never imitate source wording.
writingPatternLibrary.rule: Writing Intelligence stores technique-level lessons only. Story Dossier stores facts. Publisher text is never a style template.

weakestPattern.principle: Create headlines from the completed CE story dossier using actor + action + consequence.
weakestPattern.teachWriter: Build the headline after the article/dossier is complete; do not rewrite from publisher headlines.

writingTechniqueRegistry.purpose: Store reusable editorial craftsmanship techniques separate from article content, publisher wording, and editorial-policy weights.
boundaries: Do not store article bodies as examples to imitate.
Do not store publisher headline structures or distinctive phrasing as templates.
Store technique, conditions, failure modes, repair results, and measurable craft outcomes only.
Use Story Dossier for facts; use this registry for writing decisions.
writingTechniqueRegistry.techniqueQuestion: Which writing decision made this article pass or fail?

opening.verified_fact_first.name: Verified Fact First
opening.verified_fact_first.principle: Open with the most newsworthy verified fact before context, reaction, or analysis.
whyItWorks: Readers immediately understand what happened.
The Editor can test the lead against the dossier before the article continues.
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has who, what, when, and where.
The first paragraph can be written without publisher phrasing.

transition.fact_to_context.name: Fact To Context
transition.fact_to_context.principle: Move from verified fact to background context before any broader explanation.
useWhen: stories needing history or prior developments
legal, business, policy, and international coverage
avoidWhen: stories where context is still uncertain
whyItWorks: It keeps paragraphs from drifting into unrelated topics.
It reduces generic filler because every transition has a job.
recognizeBeforeWriting: The prior paragraph establishes a fact.
The next paragraph explains why that fact matters in this event.

evidence.classify_before_claim.name: Classify Evidence Before Claim
evidence.classify_before_claim.principle: Know whether each claim comes from an official statement, filing, independent report, eyewitness account, or single-source detail before writing it.
useWhen: court, crime, public safety, political, and business stories
whyItWorks: It separates confirmed facts from developing claims.

attribution.unique_claim_only.name: Attribute Unique Claims Only
attribution.unique_claim_only.principle: Write shared facts in CE wording and attribute outlet-specific claims only when a detail is not broadly confirmed.
avoidWhen: official-only announcements where the agency is the source
whyItWorks: It avoids over-citing every sentence while preserving traceability.
It reduces copyright risk by not leaning on publisher expression.
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier distinguishes consensus facts from unique claims.
A unique claim changes reader understanding.

headline.actor_action_consequence.name: Actor + Action + Consequence
headline.actor_action_consequence.principle: Generate the headline after the article is drafted from the dossier's main actor, action, and consequence.
useWhen: business, politics, sports, local, world, and technology
avoidWhen: stories without a clear actor or confirmed action
whyItWorks: It prevents word salad and publisher-headline imitation.
It keeps the headline anchored to the CE article instead of the RSS title.
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier identifies who acted.
Dossier identifies what changed.
A reader can see the consequence in under 12 words.

conclusion.verified_next_step.name: Verified Next Step
conclusion.verified_next_step.principle: Close with the next confirmed action, deadline, official update, or unresolved fact rather than a generic wrap-up.
useWhen: legal, government, public safety, weather, and sports coverage
avoidWhen: stories with no known next step
whyItWorks: It gives readers a concrete reason to return for updates.
It avoids ending every story with the same generic sentence.
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has an unknown, deadline, scheduled update, or official next action.

editorialComments.lesson: Seeded from existing pattern-level learning. Future updates should identify the writing decision behind each pass or failure.

quoteIntegration.claim_context.name: Claim With Context
quoteIntegration.claim_context.principle: Use quotes or reported claims only when they add an actor, evidence, dispute, or official position the article cannot state otherwise.
whyItWorks: It keeps quoted material purposeful and prevents copied article texture.
It supports accountability by linking claims to speakers.
recognizeBeforeWriting: The quote changes what is known.
The speaker or institution matters to the story.

timeline.ordered_developments.name: Ordered Developments
timeline.ordered_developments.principle: Arrange major developments by time so updates add to the original article instead of replacing it with a new generic headline.
useWhen: crime, court, weather, war, politics, and market stories
avoidWhen: stories with only one known timestamp
whyItWorks: It preserves the original CE article while showing what changed.
It helps the Brain detect whether an update is significant enough to republish.
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has original publish date plus at least one later update.

contextPlacement.after_verified_core.name: Context After Verified Core
contextPlacement.after_verified_core.principle: Place background context after the confirmed core facts so the story does not become generic perspective.
avoidWhen: urgent briefs where context would slow the key warning
whyItWorks: It prevents the article from sounding like a template.
It keeps context relevant to the current event.
recognizeBeforeWriting: The core event is already established.
The context explains the current event, not a separate topic.

factOrdering.topic_isolated_sequence.name: Topic-Isolated Fact Sequence
factOrdering.topic_isolated_sequence.principle: Order facts only from the same event cluster and reject paragraphs that introduce facts from a different story.
useWhen: top news, world, politics, business, and local
avoidWhen: roundup newsletters where multiple stories are intentionally separated
whyItWorks: It prevents mixed articles and paragraph-topic contamination.
It lets the Editor repair the earliest drift point instead of rejecting the full article blindly.
recognizeBeforeWriting: All paragraph facts map to the same story id or event cluster.
No unrelated entity appears without a dossier relationship.
